summary: Contract 5.7 and section 9 are implemented in Bots/BotController.cs (the FSM), BotSenses.cs (pure read-only geometry queries) and BotPersonality.cs (tuned presets). The bot decides every 0.1 s of sim time (decision index = floor(Tick * 10 / TickRate), so 30 decisions in 3 s at 30, 60 and 144 Hz) and outputs a heading every tick toward its current target. Home: theta among 8 directions scored over a 60 degree sector beyond the edge point E (neutral 1, rival 1.5 / 0.2 / 0.5 by style), E from GridRaster.FirstEntry, plan [E + theta depth, side leg of depth x [0.6, 1.2] toward the higher-scoring half, R = E - theta], every point clamped into the arena inset by ArenaMargin + 1. Out: smooth pursuit with Jitter redrawn per decision, owned plan points skipped, a lost R replaced by NearestOwned pushed 1 u deeper. Return triggers: trail > MaxTrailLength, own spark at TimeCut + ReactionDelay, a visible enemy head within ThreatRadius of the exposed trail for ReactionDelay, Time + D_home / PawnSpeed + 2 >= RoundDuration; then NearestOwned. Attack: the section 9 lethal-sample rule (samples every 0.5 u from L - HeadGrace - 0.3, T with turn time, G, C, E_v from NearestOwned, lethal when C < E_v - 0.2, largest lethal s_k, AttackChance x HumanAttackScale for the human), Aggressive-only harassment at AttackChance / 3, 1.5 s commitment re-aiming at the same s_k, aborts on victim home / spark / new exit / out of sight or a return trigger. Safe ring pickup (8 u, ThreatRadius around bot and ring, length budget). Lasso: one LassoChance draw per exit while charged, then a rectangular curl crossing the trail at least 3 u back (closes a b x w pocket). SenseRadius hides far enemies (head, trail, spark), the view is never mutated (checked by a fingerprint of every mutable field on every controller call over 100 rounds), all randomness comes from the bot's Rng (StateHash identical for equal seeds; a controller reused for a new Simulation resets and re-seeds). Three behaviours found while measuring, all within section 9: (1) the uncharged return often crossed the outward leg just outside the edge, and R8's loop erase then captured nothing, so the bot now applies the 'avoid crossing own trail when uncharged' rule with a detour toward the nearest crossing-free own-land entry (except when chased); (2) E could land on a one-cell notch inside the land (A2's 4-adjacency rim stairs), so holes shorter than 1 u are skipped; (3) a short home dwell (0.1 to 0.6 s) after each return brings trailing share from about 82 % to about 70 %. Cost: mean decision 0.006 ms, p99 0.08 ms (dotnet Debug). Results (asserted, seeds 1-50, 60 Hz, default config): lasso on: captures per bot 26.9 / 26.7 / 18.9 / 32.3 (Balanced, Balanced, Greedy, Aggressive), cuts in 88 % of matches, a Spark elimination in 66 %, TimeUp 94 %, coverage 38.5 %, 10.0 s for 50 rounds; lasso off: 23.2 / 24.1 / 19.9 / 31.7, cuts 96 %, Spark elimination 80 %, TimeUp 96 %, coverage 37.6 %, 9.2 s. Held-out check (seeds 101-200, not asserted): lasso on cuts 92 %, kills 68 %, TimeUp 99 %, coverage 40.7 %; lasso off 94 % / 75 % / 96 % / 38.2 %. Reported only: escapable-cut share of Spark eliminations 2.0 % (1/50) lasso on and 0 % (0/57) lasso off (held out 0/88 and 0/106; target < 10 %); trailing share per bot 71 / 70 / 75 / 65 % (target 30-75 %); human-proxy fixture alive at the end 76 % (lasso on) / 74 % (off), first 18 % / 18 % (held out: alive 63 % / 70 %, first 20 % / 18 %; target alive 35-75 %, first 15-45 %). Tests: 28 test cases (26 in the default run + 2 explicit report cases), all green in dotnet; Unity EditMode filtered on Bots_: JUnit tests=26 failures=0 errors=0 (both 10-seed round tests with invariants every tick). Full Core suite 268/268 green.
api_additions: public enum BotMode { Home, Out, Return, Attack, Ring, Idle } (current FSM state; Idle = home without a plan, e.g. not enough round time left).
BotController constants: DecisionsPerSecond = 10, AttackCommitSeconds = 1.5, RingRange = 8.0, LassoMinBack = 3.0, PlanBorderMargin = 1.0, SearchRadius = 100.0 (the section 9 numbers, named).

BotController read-only debug surface (tests, probe, debug views): BotPersonality Personality { get; }, BotMode Mode { get; }, int DecisionCount { get; }, int AttackVictim { get; } (-1 unless attacking), bool TryGetTarget(out Vec2d point) (point steered at), Vec2d EdgePoint { get; } (E of the current plan), void CopyPlan(List<Vec2d> output) (remaining plan points, last = R).
BotPersonality: no new member; the class doc comment now carries the tuned preset table.
BotSenses: internal static class (no public surface): DistanceToTrailPrefix, ScoreSector, EdgePoint (with hole skipping, MinEdgeRun = 1 u), CrossesTrail.

Test side (PainterIO.Tests.BotTests, internal): RunRound (one full bot round with invariants every tick, mutation guard, section 9 metrics), CheckInvariants (the 10.1 list without per-tick NUnit constraint objects), Summarize / RunSeeds / Summary.Format, ProbeController (decision timing + view fingerprint), BotSeed, BotOnlyLineup.
contract_issues: Section 9 'head straight for NearestOwned ... never loop' vs 'avoid crossing own trail when uncharged': with R = E - theta, the return leg enters the land only about width / (depth + 1) u beside E, and the outward leg (curved by the initial turn, jittered) often lies there, so the return crossed the first segments just outside the edge. Uncharged, R8 loop-erases the whole excursion and the return captures almost nothing (observed, then fixed). The bot applies the avoid rule on the R leg and in Return mode: when the straight way crosses an older own-trail segment (more than 1 u behind the head) and the bot is uncharged and not chased, it steers to the first own-land entry of a ray fan (+/-12 .. 80 degrees, FirstEntry) whose straight path crosses nothing, within 1.6 x the direct distance + 2 u. A chased bot always goes straight (survival first). A charged bot may cross (a pocket is a gain). Test Bots_UnchargedBotNeverCrossesItsOwnTrail.

Section 9 E = 'the first non-owned point along theta': A2's 4-adjacency Rim leaves one-cell notches inside the land, so E could be a hole 4 u inside the territory and the whole plan was built from a fake edge (observed: a 16 u excursion that captured nothing). The bot skips holes shorter than 1 u along the ray (own land again within 1 u) and keeps looking for the real edge.

Section 9 attack sampling 'k = 0, 1, ... while s_k >= 0 and P(s_k) is within AttackRadius' is read as: loop while s_k >= 0, keep the samples within AttackRadius (a sample outside does not stop the loop), so an older part of a trail passing near the bot counts. The loop stops early once even an instant intercept could not be lethal ((L - s) / (SparkSpeed - PawnSpeed) >= E_v - 0.2) and the harassment aim is known.

Section 9 harassment 'aiming at the largest reachable s_k' is read as the most recent sample within AttackRadius. Requiring also T < E_v (reachable before the victim can be home) was implemented and measured: attacks became rarer (31 instead of 95 per 50 rounds) and more successful (two thirds cut), but the share of matches with a cut fell from 92-94 % to 81 % on held-out seeds, so it was rejected.

Section 9 does not say how often AttackChance is drawn: a draw at every 0.1 s decision would make any AttackChance certain within a second. The bot draws once per enemy exit (lethal and harassment draws separately; an exit is identified by its Trail.Points[0]).

Additions not written in section 9 (documented in code): a home dwell of Range(0.1, 0.6) s after each return, heading into the land (without it trailing share was about 82 %, above the reported 30-75 % target, and bots met far more often); 15 % multiplicative score noise and a 0.02 per u transit penalty (head to E) in the direction choice; the sector score is sampled (9 rays x 1 u radial steps, weighted by radius) rather than read cell by cell; excursions shrink to end 2 s before the round end, Idle orbit when no plan fits; a trailing bot ignores a ring whose straight path crosses its own trail (same R8 reason); the lasso curl is attempted once per exit, after the plan tip is passed.

Section 9 targets on 50 seeds have a sampling spread of about 4 points (cut share) and 6 points (kill share). The section 9 rounds are chaotic, so any change in Sim, Trail or Grid reshuffles every outcome. The asserted window for the kill share (35-85 %) and the cut floor (85 %) leave room for expectations around 92 % cuts and 72 % kills, which the tuned presets give on held-out seeds; on the asserted seeds the closest margins are cut share 88 % (lasso on) and kill share 80 % (lasso off).

Bot-only lineup (not fixed by the contract): the target test uses player 0 = Balanced (the human slot), 1 = Balanced, 2 = Greedy, 3 = Aggressive, HumanIndex -1, and asserts the targets with lasso spawns both on (Tuning default) and off (runtime default).
open_issues: Final preset table (contract 5.7 order MinOut / MaxOut / MaxTrailLength / ThreatRadius / AttackRadius / AttackChance / LassoChance / Jitter / ReactionDelay): Balanced 4.5 / 10 / 34 / 6 / 7 / 0.45 / 0.5 / 0.10 / 0.30 (was 4 / 9 / 30); Greedy 5.5 / 13 / 45 / 4.5 / 5 / 0.25 / 0.8 / 0.06 / 0.40 (was 6 / 14 / 48); Aggressive 3 / 7 / 24 / 5 / 11 / 0.75 / 0.3 / 0.12 / 0.25 (unchanged); Cautious 2.5 / 5 / 16 / 8 / 4 / 0.15 / 0.4 / 0.08 / 0.35 (unchanged). SenseRadius 16, HumanAttackScale 1 everywhere. Measured on 100 held-out seeds per variant: larger Balanced and Aggressive excursions push the kill share toward 85 %, a larger ThreatRadius does not reduce kills (they come from crossings right behind a head), Aggressive AttackChance 1.0 adds as many kills as cuts, and HumanAttackScale 2 barely changes the human proxy (deliberate attacks cause about a quarter of the kills).

Balance between styles (not a section 9 target): Greedy wins 32-50 % of bot-only rounds, Aggressive 4-8 %, and Greedy dies most (deaths per player in the lasso-on run 9 / 7 / 23 / 11). About 80 % of Spark eliminations come from accidental cuts (a head crossing a trail right behind its owner's head), not from attacks; escapable deaths are almost nil.

Human-proxy fixture (reported): alive at the end 74-76 % on the asserted seeds, at the top of the 35-75 % target (63-70 % on held-out seeds); first 18-20 % (target 15-45 %). Run it with: dotnet test tools/CoreTests/PainterIO.CoreTests.csproj --artifacts-path tools/CoreTests/.art/<you> --filter "TestCategory=BotReport" --logger "console;verbosity=normal" (test BotsReport_HumanProxyFixture, explicit, about 20 s).

If a Sim, Trail or Grid change makes Bots_SeededBotOnlyRoundsMeetSection9Targets fail on a share, check the expectation on other seeds before retuning: a single 50-seed realization moves by several points (see contract_issues).

Flicker returns (A4's open issue) also happen with bots, rarely: a head grazing a notch of its own edge exits and returns within one tick (0.07 u of trail, 0 cells). They are harmless and excluded from the capture counts (only returns that captured at least one cell count).

Unity EditMode was run once through tools/unity.ps1 (agent bots, filter Bots_): 26/26, TestResults/bots_edit.xml; under Unity the round test runs 10 seeds per lasso setting and asserts only no exception and the invariants (contract 10.1). The 10-seed rounds took 1.2 s per setting in the Editor.
needs: B0 (GameSession, contract 11.2): one BotController per bot player, never shared between players; reusing it for a later round is safe (it resets and re-seeds on a new SimView or when time goes backwards). CreateRound: new BotController(p, seed) with p = BotPersonality.Preset(Balanced / Greedy / Aggressive) for players 1..3, p.HumanAttackScale = 0.3 while !SaveData.TutExitDone, and distinct bot seeds derived from the round seed (the tests use roundSeed * 7919 + player * 104729 + 17). CreateAttract: the tested bot-only lineup is player 0 Balanced, 1 Balanced, 2 Greedy, 3 Aggressive.

B6 (probe step 5, 20 s bot-controlled round): BotController(BotPersonality.Preset(BotStyle.Balanced), seed) drives the human slot without any special handling. Mode, TryGetTarget and CopyPlan are available if a debug overlay of bot intentions is wanted.
